name: How do I compare interior remodeling bids correctly?

mainEntity.name: How do I compare interior remodeling bids when each contractor prices the job differently?
mainEntity.text: How do I compare interior remodeling bids when each contractor prices the job differently?

acceptedAnswer.text: Interior remodeling bids are often difficult to compare because contractors may price the same project differently or make different assumptions about materials and scope. The right comparison starts with line items, not the bottom line. Homeowners should check whether demolition, disposal, protection, permits, design coordination, fixture allowances, and cleanup are included. They should also verify finish levels, appliance assumptions, and whether hidden conditions are covered by contingency or handled as extras. A bid that looks cheaper may simply be less complete. In practice, the best proposal is usually the one that is most specific and least ambiguous. Ask each contractor to explain differences in writing so you can compare true scope rather than guess at missing items.
acceptedAnswer.description: Compare bids by scope, exclusions, allowances, materials, labor, permits, and contingency assumptions, not just total price. A lower bid may leave out demolition, cleanup, protection, or finish upgrades. The most useful bid is the one that is clearest about what is included and what can change later.
